source: captured from Yamcs 5.13.5, an independent mission control system
note: CRC-16-CCITT values computed by Yamcs, whose CrcCciitCalculator is callable in isolation. The published check value 0x29b1 over the ASCII digits is already pinned elsewhere in this corpus; what these add is agreement on the cases no standard prints — the empty input, all zeros, and a short arbitrary sequence. Those are where an initial value or a final XOR that is wrong by a constant hides, because the check value alone can be reached by more than one wrong combination.

encode.name: interop-crc16-check-value
encode.note: The standard check value over the nine ASCII digits, independently computed. It fixes the polynomial, the initial value and the absence of a final XOR together.

encode.name: interop-crc16-of-nothing
encode.note: The CRC of an empty input is the initial value unchanged, 0xffff. No standard prints this, and it is the shortest possible test of the initial value on its own.

encode.name: interop-crc16-of-eight-zero-octets
encode.note: Eight zero octets give 0x313e rather than 0xffff, which is what distinguishes a real register from one that skips data it reads as empty.

encode.name: interop-crc16-of-a-short-sequence
encode.note: Four ascending octets, an ordinary case with no symmetry to hide a byte-order error.
